format_families.name: Explainer / breakdown
format_families.definition: Teaches how or why something works.

format_families.name: Product demo / workflow
format_families.definition: Shows a product, tool, or workflow in use.

format_families.name: Story / case study
format_families.definition: Uses an event, build update, or result as the structure.

format_families.name: Opinion / argument
format_families.definition: Presents a thesis and supporting reasoning.

format_families.name: List / framework
format_families.definition: Organizes advice or observations into a reusable structure.

format_families.name: Comparison / teardown
format_families.definition: Compares alternatives or examines something critically.

format_families.name: Unclassified
format_families.definition: Insufficient visible structure to assign a concrete format confidently.

format_patterns.name: Live product teardown
format_patterns.definition: Examines a real product or feature in public and points out how it works, succeeds, or fails.
format_patterns.inclusion_rule: The post directly inspects a named or visibly identifiable product or feature.
format_patterns.exclusion_rule: A general product opinion without a concrete inspection is not a teardown.
format_patterns.positive_example: I tested the new onboarding flow step by step; here is where activation breaks.
format_patterns.negative_example: Product teams should care more about onboarding.

format_patterns.name: Before-and-after workflow demo
format_patterns.definition: Shows a workflow before and after a tool, process, or product change.
format_patterns.inclusion_rule: The post presents a concrete old state and new state of the same workflow.
format_patterns.exclusion_rule: A standalone demo without a before/after contrast is not included.
format_patterns.positive_example: Before: 45 minutes of manual QA. After: this script catches it in two minutes.
format_patterns.negative_example: Here is a screen recording of our dashboard.

format_patterns.name: Step-by-step technical breakdown
format_patterns.definition: Explains a technical implementation or concept through ordered steps.
format_patterns.inclusion_rule: The post has a reproducible sequence of technical steps or stages.
format_patterns.exclusion_rule: A high-level technical opinion without ordered explanation is not included.
format_patterns.positive_example: How the request flows through five services: first the edge, then the queue, then the worker.
format_patterns.negative_example: Distributed systems are hard because they have many failure modes.

format_patterns.name: Build-in-public milestone story
format_patterns.definition: Narrates a concrete build, launch, customer, or operating milestone from the creator's work.
format_patterns.inclusion_rule: The post centers on a dated or measurable milestone and what happened while reaching it.
format_patterns.exclusion_rule: Generic founder advice without a specific milestone is not included.
format_patterns.positive_example: We shipped the first paid version today after six weeks of rebuilding the core flow.
format_patterns.negative_example: Founders should talk to customers every week.

format_patterns.name: Myth-busting argument
format_patterns.definition: Challenges a common belief by stating the belief and arguing for a contrary conclusion.
format_patterns.inclusion_rule: The post explicitly overturns a recognizable industry assumption.
format_patterns.exclusion_rule: A normal opinion that does not address a common belief is not included.
format_patterns.positive_example: The best growth channel is not always the one with the cheapest leads.
format_patterns.negative_example: I prefer referrals because they work well for us.

format_patterns.name: Tool-stack list
format_patterns.definition: Lists multiple tools or services used together for a defined job.
format_patterns.inclusion_rule: The post names at least three related tools in a usable stack or sequence.
format_patterns.exclusion_rule: A single tool recommendation or unrelated list is not included.
format_patterns.positive_example: Our lean research stack: Typeform for intake, Airtable for triage, and Slack for follow-up.
format_patterns.negative_example: This analytics tool is useful for early-stage teams.

format_patterns.name: Old-way versus new-way comparison
format_patterns.definition: Contrasts an established way of doing work with a newer alternative.
format_patterns.inclusion_rule: The post explicitly compares two approaches, systems, or eras.
format_patterns.exclusion_rule: A standalone recommendation without a contrasted alternative is not included.
format_patterns.positive_example: Old way: wait for a quarterly report. New way: inspect the event stream daily.
format_patterns.negative_example: Use event streams for better product decisions.

format_patterns.name: Unclassified
format_patterns.definition: A retained post whose visible structure cannot be assigned to one concrete format without guessing.
format_patterns.inclusion_rule: Use when the post is ambiguous, incomplete, or does not match a frozen pattern.
format_patterns.exclusion_rule: Do not use when one frozen pattern clearly fits.
format_patterns.positive_example: A short observation with no identifiable delivery structure.
format_patterns.negative_example: A clearly ordered technical walkthrough belongs to FP-03.

hook_patterns.name: Contrarian claim
hook_patterns.definition: Challenges a common belief or expected approach in the opening.
hook_patterns.inclusion_rule: The opening directly states or strongly implies that the usual belief is wrong.
hook_patterns.exclusion_rule: A neutral claim or preference without tension is not included.
hook_patterns.positive_example: Most startup advice about speed is backwards.
hook_patterns.negative_example: Here is what we learned this quarter.

hook_patterns.name: Specific result / proof
hook_patterns.definition: Opens with a concrete outcome, number, artifact, or observable proof.
hook_patterns.inclusion_rule: The first lines lead with a specific measurable or inspectable result.
hook_patterns.exclusion_rule: Vague claims of success without proof are not included.
hook_patterns.positive_example: We cut support response time from 18 hours to 40 minutes.
hook_patterns.negative_example: Our support process is much better now.

hook_patterns.name: Pain / problem
hook_patterns.definition: Starts from a recognizable problem, failure, or costly friction.
hook_patterns.inclusion_rule: The opening names the problem before presenting the solution or lesson.
hook_patterns.exclusion_rule: A solution-first announcement without a stated problem is not included.
hook_patterns.positive_example: Our handoffs were losing customer context every single week.
hook_patterns.negative_example: We launched a new handoff template today.

hook_patterns.name: Curiosity / open loop
hook_patterns.definition: Creates an unanswered question or delayed reveal that invites continued reading.
hook_patterns.inclusion_rule: The opening intentionally withholds the explanation or result while promising one.
hook_patterns.exclusion_rule: A complete statement with no unresolved question is not included.
hook_patterns.positive_example: One tiny change doubled our demo conversion. Guess which one.
hook_patterns.negative_example: The change that doubled demo conversion was the pricing page.

hook_patterns.name: Personal lesson
hook_patterns.definition: Leads with an individual experience, mistake, or changed belief.
hook_patterns.inclusion_rule: The opening is explicitly grounded in the creator's own experience.
hook_patterns.exclusion_rule: General advice without personal framing is not included.
hook_patterns.positive_example: I spent two years optimizing the wrong metric.
hook_patterns.negative_example: Teams should choose one metric and stick with it.

hook_patterns.name: Prediction / urgency
hook_patterns.definition: Frames the opening around what may happen next or why timing matters now.
hook_patterns.inclusion_rule: The opening makes a forward-looking or time-sensitive claim.
hook_patterns.exclusion_rule: A retrospective observation without urgency or forecast is not included.
hook_patterns.positive_example: The next wave of developer tools will be built around evaluation.
hook_patterns.negative_example: Developer tools have changed a lot over the last decade.

hook_patterns.name: Unclassified
hook_patterns.definition: The opening is missing or does not confidently fit one frozen hook pattern.
hook_patterns.inclusion_rule: Use when the hook is ambiguous or no approved hook is visible.
hook_patterns.exclusion_rule: Do not use when one frozen hook clearly fits.
hook_patterns.positive_example: A post beginning mid-story without enough context to identify its hook.
hook_patterns.negative_example: A post that clearly opens with a measurable result belongs to HP-02.

labeling_rules: Format families are navigation context only; concrete patterns are the scored units.
Assign one primary format pattern and at most one primary hook per scored post.
Use unclassified rather than forcing an uncertain label.
Do not encode creator identity, topic, or performance in a pattern label.
Do not create format-hook combination patterns.
Freeze labels before inspecting performance results.
